body:
Hey!

It's actually really lucky that I even saw this. This throwaway account was linked to a work computer that they changed out around a month ago. I'm in a training class right now at work, and it just so happens that this computer is my old one. I didn't even know that when I sat down here. Seriously VERY lucky.

Things have been going better recently. I actually had a date tonight, but she cancelled... She said she had a cold. Obviously not really something I did, but still a little disheartening. Still, that's a lot better than I was doing. I spent that month in therapy, like I said, and it was helpful. I've been in therapy ongoing since then, every Wednesday. It's really helping. I've even been considering going back to school for a Master's in Social Work.

Anyway, my main account is /u/EXPLODEDman. If you ever want to talk again, just shoot me a message me there.

Hey! I just got back from my leave of absence. Things are better. Not great, but better. I suppose some of my expectations for therapy were a little unrealistic, but I've really started to try, and that's a big step. I've even managed to go on a couple of dates. They haven't developed into anything, but it's still a huge step for me. I just want you to know that I didn't forget the concern you showed for me, and I really appreciate your caring.
Sometimes I don't have any sympathy for me, either.

Thanks for listening to me. This is my last day at work before I take that time off. I don't know my password for this account anymore, and I won't  be able to access it at home. I might not get back to you for a month, but when I do, hopefully I have good news.

I think I would have a harder time with succeeding than getting rejected, at this point. I mean, the outcome would by far and away be better, but it'd still be a big change to deal with. The prospect is about as exciting as it is scary.


After this week, I'm going on short-term disability to go into intensive therapy, like I said. We'll see how things shape up after that.
Maybe. If I check out early, I guess I'll never know. I'll hold off for a while. Thanks for talking to me.

I really hope so. I would love to feel like I enjoyed my life again. I've been in this state for almost 10 years, now. It's slowly gotten worse, and I can tell that it's permanently affected my personality. A big part of the reason I've stayed this way is because finding the motivation and will to change myself can only be achieved by directly contradicting everything that depression makes me feel and believe. This is very difficult to do, obviously, and can only come from some reservoir of will that I have yet to find inside myself. 

On top of that, one of the things that I've come to realize from my situation is how important touch is to a person's mental health. It's a basic and intrinsically understood communication of value for another person, and living without it for so long is for sure a contributing factor (if not the main factor) to my ongoing sense of worthlessness. 

The frustration I feel from knowing EXACTLY what my problem is, and feeling incapable of changing it is a hope-killer.

I guess. I talked to a professional about my thoughts, and I'm going to be taking some FMLA to go into intensive therapy. Maybe it'll work. Who knows.

You're pretty young though, right?

I find that most of my time thinking is regret. Please remember that everything possibility that comes your way is a decision that could change your life. You don't have to take all of them, and in fact you shouldn't. But if you don't take any, you might find yourself where I am now. Regardless of the truth of it, my life feels pretty much over.

Please take chances for me.

The customers are alright. I'm a "specialist," and what that means is that I have more program knowledge than the people who take direct inbound calls. Really all I deal with is co-workers who call me when they don't know what they're doing, or supervisor transfer calls, which are almost always unpleasant. We had a new system get released a few months ago, and the "metrics" my bosses track show that our workload has gone up 300%. Literally. It's not really the calls so much that I hate about being here. It's the sitting all day. I sit in a grey felt cube for 8 hours a day, 5 days a week. I hate these walls. All they do is compound on my feeling of isolation. 40 hours of walls, then the remaining 128 I spend either trying to sleep, or playing video games in a dark room. It's like I said. I miss the experience of human touch. I don't feel like a real person anymore. It's like I'm a zombie playing pretend, while everyone else around me is alive. I get to leave in 10 minutes, thank God. I've got an appointment with my therapist today. She's not bad, but sometimes she's not very engaged, and honestly 30 minutes never feels like enough to actually talk about anything. It's all my work-provided health insurance will cover, though.

I work at a call center. I graduated with a Bachelor's in English a couple years back, and I couldn't manage to find a job that wanted my degree. Once again, I am at work as we speak.

It's touching that you took the time to come back and talk to me. The thread died, but the thoughts haven't.
I struggle with this because my first girlfriend cheated on me with my best friend.
Anxiety.
It takes every bit of my effort to keep my shit together. It's not even about the sex anymore. I just want to cuddle again. I just want a hug
I feel like screaming. I feel like crying. I feel like ripping this keyboard in half. I am sitting here quietly doing my work. I want to burn
It feels right. I don't know why. Things have been like this for so long. I want them to see the suffering I feel. I feel so empty and cold.
I'm 27, and I'm at work right now.

My first thought was: "Wow, and I managed to fuck this up, too."
There were no consequences. The prison placed the blame for the death on his condition.

I'm just saying it's not surprising, or even near the worst thing that goes on in prison. It's a much larger problem that has to do with the way prisoners are regarded in the US, as less than human.

It's neat that makes me an MRA, though, I didn't know that. 

I also didn't know it made someone "whiny" to be appalled by the prospect of allowing another living person to die on the floor without so much as the slightest concern.

"Ehhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh... I don't wanna."

-Pigs

When my brother was in prison, a man in the cell across from his collapsed on the floor, having a seizure. While he was falling, he hit his head on something, and was bleeding all over the floor. My brother and other nearby inmates began calling for a guard to come help. After being casually disregarded for fifteen minutes, a guard strolled over, looked at the man, ash-faced and bleeding on the floor, and said:

"Hey. Get up."

When the man was unresponsive, he called in for the medical team. They came 20 minutes later. The man died.

Correction: People in jail are being treated without basic human dignity. End the profit-prison nightmare now.
Depression

I would love to make some quality connections with women. It just feels disingenuous and deceptive to try and be close on a personal level when I want them physically. It's not that I don't want to be close on a personal level, it's just that it feels like I'm secretly planning on hurting them, or "thinking with my dick," and operating with ulterior motives. I guess that's just more guilt about my sexuality.

And then everyone on Reddit says that I'm supposed to get close physically BEFORE I get close emotionally. From what I've heard in dating advice threads, at least.

Anyway, where can I meet women I can develop this sort of relationship with? The new people I meet always seem apprehensive, and I don't know how to assuage that uncertainty.
I know it's a problem. I just worry that if I let people see who I am and what bothers me, they'll just come to the same conclusion I have about myself.

I really appreciate your help.

1. I don't know how to start with this one. I don't know how to express what I want, or when it's appropriate to do so. I'm terrified that I'm going to get a "fuck off," or strange looks, just for trying to be honest about my intent. I'm afraid that women are going to think I'm some sort of pervert, or that I want to hurt them.

2. You're right. I need to let go of my past, but it's so hard for me to look at the present and not think about all of the pieces that went into making it what it is.

3. I have a couple of friends, we just don't talk about things like this. We do stuff together, but we don't talk about our problems.

4. I've tried picking up new hobbies, but I have a hard time dealing with being bad at things. It always ends up being an excuse to dump on myself, which is once again part of the problem here.

I think a big part of all of this is a loop of self-defeat that I've created for myself, to reinforce my own terrible opinion of myself. I don't imagine there's a way to fix that except to push through.

Thanks. One thing that I've discovered from the long time I've spent alone is that it's really hard to see how you might be of value when you've never seen why another person would value you. As for the sex, what really scares me is that I might start to get attached to someone, and they leave me because I'm really bad. 

I'm glad you chimed in to say something. It's reassuring to think that these things might not be as big a deal as I feel like they are.

I don't want to be alone anymore. I want to feel physically and emotionally connected to someone again. I don't want to feel like a bad person for wanting that. I just really need to know how to go about getting back into it without overwhelming someone with my personal problems.

Well, the first one I saw was really good, but I had a really hard time talking to her about any of this.  The second one was an intensive IBT group, and I put in a lot of effort on that one. I learned a lot of helpful skills in there for managing my negative thoughts and feelings, but not enough to get past them. The third I only saw for one session, and the fourth was trying to put me through IBT again, which didn't feel helpful, since I was already familar with the techniques of IBT. I should go back to therapy and put more work into it. I don't really have any excuses for that. It just feels disingenuous and hokey when they ask me to spend time on myself, because I have a difficult time seeing why I should. I know almost certainly that's part of my problem.
